newsitem.title: GREECE: Princess Diana eludes press on Greek island cruise.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana eludes press on Greek island cruise.

text.p: Princess Diana eluded scores of paparazzi for a third day on Monday as they scoured the Greek islands for a glimpse of the world's most photographed woman, believed to be holidaying incognito in the Aegean.

Despite efforts that would make their British tabloid colleagues proud, Greece's celebrity-crazed press hounds have so far failed to sniff out Diana, who arrived at Athens airport by private jet Friday night and then disappeared.

Reports have put the princess, whose romance with Egyptian playboy Dodi Al Fayed has made world headlines, all over the Aegean Sea. Some even say her Greek island-hopping cruise is over and she has left for Switzerland.

More than 50 reporters, cameramen and photographers rushed to the small island of Inousses, off the north Aegean island of Chios, in hopes she would go there to visit her friends, the London-based Lemos shipping family.
Their yacht, the Mistral Blue, is docked at Inousses but shipowner Panayotis Lemos told reporters he was not expecting her.
"We don't know where Princess Diana is," he told Greek television. "We don't know whether she will come here."

While scores of paparazzi waited at Inousses, Greece's two major TV channels, Antenna and Mega, appeared to agree that Diana sailed along the eastern coast of the Peloponnese, stopping at the beach of Kipparissi and the islands of Spetses and Kythira.
"She was wearing a red baseball cap, a blue dress and pink canvas shoes," a Spetses shopowner who claimed to have seen the princess told Antenna TV. "She even cracked me a smile."
The TV channels agreed that Diana travelled by helicopter to the small airport on Kythira, where she boarded a private Lear jet and left for the Swiss town of Lugano.
"We saw her getting out of the helicopter and getting on the Lear jet," Kythira airport commander Yannis Halaris told the private Mega TV. "They asked for clearance to land in Lugano."
Despite their failure to locate the princess, Greek newspapers had a field day with her Greek visit.

The liberal Athens daily Eleftherotypia published blurred photographs of an undistinguishable woman sitting on a beach, saying the paper got them from a reader who took snapshots of Diana, shocked to see her in Kiparissi.

Athens dailies feature various eyewitness reports placing the princess on the islands of Mykonos and Andros, and rumours that Diana was on the Turkish coast for a secret rendezvous with the Egyptian playboy.
Al Fayed, 41, whose father owns the luxury Harrods stores, has been in the news since he was photographed romancing Diana on board a yacht in the Mediterranean last month.
He has vowed to fight a lawsuit brought against him by an American model who alleges she was ditched in favour of Diana. The princess was divorced last year from heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles.
